::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
The $10 billion fab that started China's 12-inch era paper boom and ended it: GF halted funding Oct 2018 amid its own IPO delay; the government-built shell stood empty; formal closure with severance for the last 74 employees May 2020; a reported revival by Intel was shelved Nov 2021; a 2020 claim that ex-SK Hynix VP Choi Jin-seok's 成都高真科技 would take the shell for DRAM is not verified as ever materializing.
:::

**Chinese name:** 格芯（成都）集成电路制造有限公司（未建成） (Géxīn (Chéngdū))

## What does this facility make?

Nothing — the site never brought production tools in; it was sealed January 2019.

## Why does it matter?

This tracker previously only footnoted GF Chengdu's absence in About; it is now a proper Cancelled entry — the closure of GF Chengdu is the pivot point after which every surviving 12-inch project became state-financed, and the empty shell became the cautionary reference in every subsequent local-government fab pitch.

## Project Timeline

- **Feb 2017** — GF-Chengdu JV announced — at the time the largest planned 12-inch logic fab in mainland China
- **Oct 2018** — GF cancels remaining investment; tools removed early 2019, site sealed
- **Nov 2021** — SCMP: Intel shelts takeover of the abandoned plant
